report.source_text: a series of thromboembolic laboratory tests were conducted, including aCL, aβ2GPI, LAC, protein C (PC), protein S (PS), antithrombin III activity (AT-III), antinuclear antibody and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies ( Table 1 ). Although only aβ2GPI IgA was positive, it raised our suspicions of APS.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old woman presented with 20 days of language difficulty, unresponsiveness, apathy, and cognitive decline. Brain MRI demonstrated a chronic cortical infarct in the left frontal lobe with no arterial stenosis or classical cerebrovascular risk factors. Initial thrombosis and classical antiphospholipid antibody tests showed only aβ2GPI IgA positivity, insufficient for classical APS diagnosis. Subsequent immunological testing found positive antibodies to vimentin/cardiolipin complex and anti-annexin A5 antibody, supporting SN-APS diagnosis. Long-term anticoagulation and antiplatelet therapy were initiated with no stroke recurrence.
